native_retrieval.title: CJP's parliament march from Jantar Mantar: India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown - BBC
native_retrieval.snippet: # India's 'cockroach' protest continues a day after police crackdown. Thousands have gathered again in the Indian capital Delhi a day after a police crackdown on supporters of India's Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a youth-led movement seeking education reforms and resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. Tens of thousands of young men and women had turned up for Monday's protest and tried to march on parliament, defying a police ban. Police said 118 of their personnel were also injured and 70 protesters have been detained. Police and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government have not commented on the use of sticks and tear gas against protesters. The meeting took place against the backdrop of tens of thousands of people turning up from all over the country to participate in the CJP's call to march to parliament on the opening day of the monsoon session.

native_retrieval.title: Modi Has Few Good Options to Quell India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protests - Bloomberg.com
native_retrieval.snippet: # Modi Has Few Good Options to Quell India’s ‘Cockroach’ Protests. ## **Takeaways** by Bloomberg AISubscribe. What started as a satirical online movement two months ago has turned into one of India’s biggest student protests in years, sparking scenes of violent clashes in New Delhi. And Prime Minister Narendra Modi has few good options to stop them. Launched in May by young organizers with little political experience, the Cockroach Janta Party managed to draw crowds of students, parents and professionals into the heart of India’s capital, where they jumped police barricades and faced tear gas and baton charges in an attempt to march to the parliament on Monday. They started by demanding the resignation of India’s education minister after a series of exam scandals, but frustrations quickly morphed into broader anger at Modi’s government. native_retrieval.title: Police attack Cockroach activists as thousands march on Indian parliament - Al Jazeera
native_retrieval.snippet: *More than 10,000 protesters braved tear gas and baton charges in their largest challenge yet to PM Modi’s government.*. Police have fired tear gas and attacked supporters of the youth-led Cockroach movement with canes and baton charges as more than 10,000 marched towards India’s parliament in New Delhi in the largest protest yet demanding the resignation of the education minister and a crackdown on corruption in the exam system. The march on Monday by the protesters who ironically call themselves the Cockroach Janta Party to mock the name of the ruling party of Prime Minister Narendra Modi was even bigger than expected, with numbers swelled by anger at Saturday’s forcible hospitalisation of veteran 59-year-old activist Sonam Wangchuk, who has been on hunger strike for three weeks in solidarity with the movement. Modi’s government, shaken by the emergence of the Cockroach movement in May, offered a minor concession by inviting two activists to meet a senior cabinet minister for talks.

native_retrieval.title: India’s Cockroach protests: Rahul Gandhi detained after calling for PM Modi to resign - The Guardian
native_retrieval.snippet: Opposition leader taken away after accusing Narendra Modi of ‘destroying the future of India’s youth’ during protest in solidarity with cockroach movement. Indian police briefly detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday during protests calling for prime minister Narendra Modi’s resignation, in solidarity with the new youth-led cockroach party movement. Gandhi, the leader of India’s Congress party, staged a sit-in outside Modi’s house on Tuesday afternoon, stating that Modi must resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth”. His protest took place as thousands of students were gathered at a separate site in central Delhi, the day after a huge protest calling for the resignation of Modi’s education minister was met with brutality by Delhi police, including baton attacks and teargas. Gandhi said his party was taking their protest directly to the prime minister’s house, after the Modi government refused to take up the issues of the students and the alleged “brutality unleashed on students” in parliament.
